response: Evidence and review overlap analysis. Shared evidence: all four hypotheses cite no task-level evidence records yet — their common grounding is the run objective's stated failure modes and the calibration observations referenced inside review texts (default self-testing, 5-13 tool calls of a 15-turn cap, saturation at easy difficulty). This uniform grounding means evidence overlap cannot differentiate the arms; differentiation lives entirely in review content. Review overlap: initial, full, deep-verification, and simulation reviews agree across arms on three recurring findings — (1) the shared unmeasured premise that spec-compliance failures dominate baseline errors, (2) compliance-depth unobservability without transcript covariates, (3) effect concentration on requirement-dense tasks. These are family-level, not arm-level, weaknesses; they should propagate to the meta-review rather than justify rejecting any single arm. Contradictions: none between reviews of different arms; one productive tension within reviews of test-first (higher ceiling on never-encoded omissions vs unbounded downside under all-pass grading), resolved consistently by both debate orderings in favor of bounded-risk arms at this sample size. Deduplication signals: checklist and re-read overlap strongly (same mechanism, different dose); reviews and both pairwise matches treat re-read as the dominated variant — mark the pair with a dose-variant edge, keep both for dose-response interpretation, but any roster pruning should drop re-read first. Diversity gap confirmed by reviews: no arm targets algorithmic-inability failures; the family cannot adjudicate that failure class regardless of experiment outcome.
